extracted.intended_audience: ERC peer reviewers (Panel Chairs, Panel Members, Panel Evaluators, Remote Referees) for the Synergy Grant call
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for carrying out the panel-based, three-step peer review evaluation of ERC Synergy Grant full proposals (Steps 1–3), including writing individual assessments, participating in panel meetings and interviews, and drafting panel comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence as the sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of proposals for funding by the ERCEA is a result of a panel-based, peer review evaluation with excellence as the sole criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels must evaluate proposals only against excellence (no other political or policy considerations). All panel comments and scoring must reflect this single overarching criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — ground‑breaking nature and ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels will primarily evaluate the ground‑breaking nature and ambition of the research project and whether the proposal enables substantial advances at the frontiers of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed work could become a benchmark on a global scale, enable breakthroughs not possible by individual PIs alone, and stem from cross‑fertilisation, new productive lines, new methods/techniques, unconventional approaches or interface research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — novelty, interdisciplinarity and transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The project should demonstrate novelty, cross‑disciplinary/multi‑disciplinary potential, and transformative impact (e.g., new methods, unconventional approaches, interface research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the project differs from the current state of knowledge and whether it has potential to be transformative or become a global benchmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Part B1 content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B1 (Extended Synopsis / Part I) should present the envisaged research, lay out the current state of knowledge, explain the scientific question and objectives, and present the overall approach or research strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All essential information for judging whether to pass to Step 2 must be included in Part B1; Panel Members act as generalists in Step 1 and base decisions on this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Part B2 content and implementation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B2 (including Part II of the Scientific proposal) must include a detailed explanation of project implementation: research methodology, work plan, risk assessment and mitigation measures, justification for requested budget and resources, and any additional necessary background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Step 2 reviewers (generalists and specialists) evaluate both the scientific case and the soundness of the implementation plan and resource justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergy Group — complementarities, synergies and added value
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the extent to which the Synergy Grant Group demonstrates it brings together complementary skills, knowledge and resources (skills, experience, expertise, disciplines, teams) necessary to address the proposed research question and create added value over PIs acting alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clear evidence that the group configuration is essential to achieving the proposed breakthroughs and that synergies are credible and described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk and risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are expected to be risky but must show that the risk and how it will be managed are well thought through and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether risks are identified, realistic, and whether mitigation and contingency plans are adequate and credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigators — intellectual capacity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent have the Principal Investigators demonstrated the ability to conduct ground‑breaking research and provided evidence of creative and original thinking?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate PIs' past achievements, originality, and indications of future potential to lead the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigators — expertise and capacity to execute
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the PIs have the required scientific expertise and capacity (including track records, CVs) to successfully execute the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the team has the technical skills, leadership, resources and prior achievements that make successful execution likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group composition — bringing together necessary know‑how
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the Synergy Grant Group successfully demonstrates in the proposal that it brings together the know‑how necessary to address the research question (skills, experience, expertise, disciplines, teams) based on the Extended Synopsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for complementary competences and clear roles/tasks for each PI and team, with justification of why this exact grouping is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring categories and their meanings (A invited / A not invited / B / C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal receives a panel score: A invited (excellent and ranked high enough to pass to next step), A not invited (excellent but not ranked high enough), B (high quality but not sufficient to pass), C (not sufficient quality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels must assign one of these scores at each step and explain decisions in panel comments. Step‑specific consequences (e.g., feedback given, resubmission restrictions) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking and budgetary cut‑offs in selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Retention to the next step is limited by budgetary cut‑offs (Step 1: up to 7x panel budget; Step 2: up to 3x panel budget) and final funding depends on call budget and normalised accumulated budget consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels must take into account these quantitative constraints when deciding which 'A' proposals to pass to the next step; panel comments may reflect budgetary reasons for rejecting otherwise strong proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel comments — requirements and separation from budget recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel comments should clearly explain the reason(s), respecting the ERC evaluation criterion, which make(s) the proposal succeed or fail. Scientific feedback must be clearly distinct from budget recommendations to the ERCEA (the latter are binding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel comments are a conclusive, panel‑approved document; they must document weaknesses revealed in discussion, be consistent with individual reviews, and may be edited for readability or to remove clerical/inappropriate content only under strict rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Assessment Reports / Individual reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must provide individual assessments (written reviews) in the online system for assigned proposals at each relevant step, covering strengths and weaknesses and justifying marks and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual reviews form the basis for panel discussions and applicants receive these alongside panel comments; differences of opinion among reviewers are legitimate and may be useful to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Reviewer and panel drafting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal has a Lead Reviewer who introduces the proposal to the panel, is responsible for drafting the panel comment (in conjunction with the panel) and for reflecting main points of panel discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead Reviewer drafts panel comments for certain categories at specified steps (e.g., A not invited and B at Step 2, all proposals at Step 3); panel must agree and approve final version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion threshold — numerical mark guiding need for discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that receive a numerical mark of 3.5 or lower from all reviewers do not need to be discussed unless the panel explicitly decides otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels may choose to discuss low‑scoring proposals in exceptional cases; reviewers should be aware of this threshold when assigning marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget review and justification at Step 3
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 3 the panel analyses the budget and its justification and may recommend reduction of requested grant if expenses (excluding salary costs) are not fully justified; recommendations must be documented and explained in panel comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cuts must be case‑by‑case (no across‑the‑board cuts) and should be based on analysis of necessary resources to carry out the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of voting vs consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Consensus decisions are preferred, but panels may expedite ranking by use of a voting system (e.g., majority vote); Panel Chair/Member under conflict may not discuss or vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If voting is used each Panel Member has one vote per proposal; the panel must ensure fairness and record outcomes accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest — declaration and list of conflict situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare absence of conflicts of interest; a displayed list of conflicts includes being a PI or team member, involvement in preparation, personal or financial benefit, employment/contract with participant in last 3 years, director/trustee/partner roles, collaboration within 5 years, mentor/mentee relationships, family/close personal ties, scientific rivalry/hostility, NCP or EEN roles, membership of EU Programme Committee, or any other situation that could preclude impartial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts must confirm no conflicts when accepting and when submitting reviews; Panel Chairs should avoid assigning proposals to conflicted reviewers; experts who become aware of conflict must inform ERCEA and stop working until instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for exclusion of independent experts by applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request up to four specific persons not to act as peer reviewers for their proposal; such requests are treated confidentially and experts may be excluded if ERCEA can still secure qualified evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an excluded expert is a panel member they will be informed confidentially; exclusion of a Panel Chair may lead to consulting the Vice Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Code of Conduct — performing the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts must work independently and in a personal capacity (not on behalf of any organisation), perform tasks confidentially and fairly, apply highest ethical standards, follow instructions and time schedules, not delegate work, notify the contracting authority if approached by persons linked to a proposal, observers must not evaluate, and experts must not be (or become) involved in projects they have assessed for the contracting authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaches may be qualified as grave professional misconduct with contractual consequences including termination; experts must perform to the best of their professional abilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Code of Conduct — impartiality and exclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartiality obligations include explicit automatic conflict situations and graduated exclusions: (1) exclusion from evaluation for a proposal (e.g., director/employee of participating entity), (2) exclusion for a proposal and all competing proposals (e.g., involved in preparation, would benefit, close family ties), (3) exclusion from entire call (e.g., member of advisory group preparing work programmes, NCP or EU Programme Committee member), and potential exclusions based on recent employment/collaboration within 3–5 years or other situations casting doubt on impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences vary by situation; contracting authority may exceptionally allow participation under strict documented conditions; experts must declare conflicts and stop work if conflict arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Code of Conduct — confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts must keep confidential all sensitive information disclosed during the contract and for five years after last payment; they may use such information only to implement the contract, must not disclose evaluation details or names of other experts, and must not communicate with applicants except as organised by the contracting authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documentation is provided electronically, experts are responsible for protecting it and returning/erasing/destroying sensitive information after evaluation if instructed; confidentiality ceases only if contracting authority releases expert, information becomes public elsewhere, or disclosure is required by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Code of Conduct — data protection and personal data security
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts must process personal data only on documented instructions, only for the duration and purposes in the contract, ensure protection of personal data proportionate to risk, not disclose personal data without authorisation, report personal data breaches immediately, and delete or return personal data at the end of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts must cooperate with the contracting authority on data protection compliance and adopt appropriate technical/organisational measures to avoid breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel deliverables and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel outputs include a panel report (methodology, reflections, possible recommendations), annexes (ranked list, conflicts considered, panel comments for feedback, list of delivered reviews, list of approved Remote Referees, panel recommendations to Scientific Council) and Evaluation Reports for applicants (panel recommendation/ranking range, panel comment, individual reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Members must ensure that panel comments and reports are accurate, reflect the panel's methodology and decisions, and are consistent with the ERC Rules of submission and evaluation; ERCEA may edit panel comments only to improve readability or remove clerical/inappropriate errors without affecting results.
